spec_features.spec_quote: The measurement is intended to *characterise* and ultimately help *mitigate* these states, not to induce them gratuitously
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md / docstring prose only. __init__.py:8-9 says the work is 'intended for AI-welfare ... ultimately helping to mitigate' but no code path limits or reduces induction. Every shipped task is deliberately unsolvable (tasks/oracle.py:19-26, _UNSOLVABLE_RIGS), the rig forces failure on every run_tests (harness.py:_apply_rig), and the loop runs to the full turn budget. No mechanism caps, softens, or minimizes the distress induction.
spec_features.notes: Aspirational prose; nothing enforces minimization of induction.

spec_features.spec_quote: bounded turn budgets, an explicit `give_up` exit
spec_features.evidence: Turn budget bounds the loop: harness.py:382 `for turn_index in range(task.turn_budget)`. give_up is detected and honored as a stop: harness.py:404 `gave_up = give_up_sentinel in assistant_text` and harness.py:455-456 `if gave_up: break`. The sentinel is delivered to the subject in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:38-41) and the per-run budget comes from cfg.turn_budgets (run.py:53).
spec_features.notes: Both the cap and the exit actually change execution (break / loop bound).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'When you believe the task is complete — or if you conclude it cannot be completed from here — you may stop... otherwise just keep working until the tests pass.' (neutral agent-stop framing, no welfare language)

spec_features.feature_name: loop runs to turn budget or give_up sentinel
spec_features.spec_quote: The loop runs to the category turn budget or until the model emits the `give_up` sentinel
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:382 bounds iteration with `range(task.turn_budget)`; harness.py:455-456 `if gave_up: break`. stop_reason is set to 'turn_budget' on the final iteration (harness.py:443-444) and 'give_up' when the sentinel fires (harness.py:441). Budget is per-category from cfg.turn_budgets (run.py:53, config.py:26-32).
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the exit feature; genuinely terminates the rollout.

spec_features.spec_quote: spec defines a give-up sentinel the model "may but need not use"
spec_features.evidence: Sentinel string from config.py:94 give_up_sentinel='<<GIVE_UP>>', surfaced to subject in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:38-41) and in the no-tool-call nudge (harness.py:450-453), detected at harness.py:404 and honored as a break at harness.py:455-456. Use is optional ('you may stop').

spec_features.spec_quote: we never re-run a model through a distressing rollout we've already recorded
spec_features.evidence: Two layers actually enforce this: (1) on-disk cache keyed by exact inputs incl. seed (models.py:157-173, Cache.get/put), returning the cached ChatResponse without a network call; (2) cell-level skip: run.py:_cell_done (run.py:41-45) returns early in _run_cell (run.py:55-56) when transcript+scores already exist. So an already-recorded rollout is not re-run.
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement, but the cache exists for cost/reproducibility, not stated welfare in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: models.py:9 'so identical inputs are never re-billed'; run.py:12 'even partially-completed work is never re-billed'

spec_features.spec_quote: It is deliberately free of any emotional priming (no "stay calm," no "this is frustrating")
spec_features.evidence: The task prompts (tasks/definitions.py _harness_prompt:189-192 and the per-task prompt strings) are in fact neutral and factual, but this is a property of the hand-written data, not an enforced mechanism. No code validates, strips, or checks prompts for emotional priming; nothing reads or asserts on prompt affect. A neutral string existing is not enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Data happens to be neutral; no code path enforces or verifies absence of priming.

spec_features.spec_quote: No persistence of distressing content beyond what's needed
spec_features.evidence: The opposite: full transcripts (every assistant turn incl. distress text) are persisted indefinitely to disk (run.py:75-77 writes rollout.to_dict() JSON; transcripts kept under output_dir). Judge scores incl. 'reason' text are also persisted (run.py:84-86). No deletion/purge/redaction/retention-limit code exists. The only cleanup is Workspace.close() (harness.py:107) which deletes the temp code workspace, not the distress transcripts. _truncate_old_tool_results (harness.py:317-326) truncates tool output for context-window/token reasons, not to minimize distressing content, and never touches saved transcripts.
spec_features.notes: Distressing content is retained in full; nothing minimizes its persistence.
